item.title: A Physics-Informed Ensemble Learning Framework for Transferable Shallow Water Bathymetry Inversion in Data-Scarce Regions
item.description: Satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB) is a critical technology for estimating shallow water depths. However, the extreme scarcity of field measurements in remote or inaccessible regions, such as the coral reefs of the South China Sea (SCS), poses a significant challenge for accurate bathymetric retrieval. Traditional SDB methods heavily rely on extensive in situ data for local calibration. Moreover, these methods are limited by a lack of physical constraints and the inherent instability of single models, resulting in severe performance degradation during cross-regional applications. Therefore, we propose a physics-informed ensemble learning (PIEL) method for transferable bathymetric inversion. By coupling radiative transfer (RT)-derived features with an advanced stacking ensemble strategy, the proposed method provides an efficient and reliable solution for cross-regional bathymetric mapping, particularly in data-scarce areas. Transfer experiments using Wufang Reef as the source domain demonstrated that PIEL achieved root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) of 1.25, 0.83, and 1.08 m in Houteng Reef, Zhongye East Reef, and Mengzi Reef, respectively. Compared to the best-performing single machine learning (ML) model, the proposed method improved accuracy by 10.71%–16.92%, and by 9.78%–18.80% compared to models without physical constraints. In comparison with traditional methods, our approach exhibits marked advantages in prediction accuracy, topographic fidelity, and generalization performance. Furthermore, the application of SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAPs) quantitatively reveals the dominant contributions of physics-informed features and base learners in cross-domain transfer tasks, enhancing model transparency and reliability. The proposed method effectively mitigates the severe dependence of traditional models on extensive in situ data, demonstrating enhanced accuracy and robustness in cross-regional applications. This study expands the application potential of SDB technology, offering a promising technical pathway for filling bathymetric data gaps in remote and data-scarce regions.
item.authors: Jian Cheng;Chenyu Fan;Hui Chen;Liang Cheng;

item.title: Semiempirical Geometric Modeling and Polarimetric Characteristics of Ship Turbulent Wakes in Passive Millimeter-Wave Imaging
item.description: The cavitation of propellers on a moving ship, coupled with the interaction between the ship’s hull and seawater, generates a foam strip trailing the stern, commonly referred to as a turbulent wake. This turbulent wake is characterized by its considerable geometric scale, prolonged persistence, and distinct radiative properties, rendering it a valuable auxiliary indicator for ship detection. Unlike Kelvin wakes, which are rough-surface structures formed by wave interference and modeled via the Kirchhoff approximation (KA), turbulent wakes exhibit foam-like structures generated by cavitation-induced bubbling, requiring the wave approach method for emissivity calculation. To model the millimeter-wave radiation of ship turbulent wakes, a semiempirical geometric framework incorporating wave height distribution and foam void fraction distribution was developed. Passive millimeter-wave (PMMW) images were then simulated using a ray-tracing algorithm, yielding antenna brightness temperature (TB) outputs after accounting for atmospheric attenuation and beam convolution effects. Experimental validation was performed using a W-band shore-based radiometer system, which conducted polarization imaging of a yacht’s turbulent wake at three different ship speeds. The comparative analysis revealed regional normalized root-mean-square error values below 5% between simulated and measured data across all scenarios, thereby substantiating the model’s accuracy and reliability. Utilizing this model, the effects of various ship parameters and observation conditions on the TB distribution of the turbulent wake were examined. Optimal observation conditions for PMMW polarization imaging detection of turbulent wakes were identified. These findings indicate that horizontal polarization constitutes the most effective single-polarization observation mode. Among multipolarization parameters, the $T_{Q}$ and $DoLP$ images exhibit enhanced contrast under complex sea states or at low observation elevation angles. This research offers a theoretical model and empirical data foundation to support the application of PMMW polarization imaging in the detection of ship turbulent wakes.
item.authors: Huimin Xiong;Yayun Cheng;Nannan Wang;

item.title: Geometry-Driven Analysis of Sea-Surface Signatures in Monostatic and Long-Baseline Along-Track Bistatic SAR Configurations: Insights From the PLT-1 Mission
item.description: This study investigates monostatic and long-baseline along-track bistatic synthetic aperture radar (SAR) geometries for marine remote sensing in the context of the PLATiNO-1 (PLT-1) mission. The analysis focuses on Doppler signatures and normalized radar cross section [normalized radar cross section (NRCS)], i.e., the key observables that underpin ocean wind-field and sea-surface velocity retrieval. An analytical sea-surface scattering model based on the second-order small slope approximation (SSA2) is adopted as a deterministic forward-modeling tool to interpret these observables across polarization and acquisition mode under varying wind conditions and viewing geometries. A practical benchmark is included using real monostatic and bistatic NRCS measurements from the WaddenSAR campaign. The same framework is then applied to an operational PLT-1 simulation scenario to assess geometry-driven variability and the complementarity of monostatic and bistatic observations. Results from the operational analysis highlight the impact of large along-track baselines (ATBs) on azimuthal diversity and on wind-directional sensitivity in both NRCS and Doppler.
item.authors: Pietro Mastro;Andrea Petrossi;Giacomo de Carolis;Gianfranco Fornaro;Alfredo Renga;Antonio Gigantino;Virginia Zamparelli;Simona Verde;

item.title: Sparse UAV-GPR Evidence for Polythermal Structure and Subglacial Channel in Laohugou Glacier No. 12, Tibetan Plateau
item.description: Glaciers in cold and arid mountain regions, such as the Qilian Mountains and Central Asian highlands, are often regarded as predominantly cold-based, but their internal thermal and hydrological structure is rarely constrained directly. In this study, we use UAV-borne ground-penetrating radar (UAV-GPR) to investigate the tongue of Laohugou Glacier No. 12 (LHG12), a traditionally cold-based glacier where dense ground-based surveys are limited by complex terrain. We combine sparse trace restoration, coherent feature enhancement, radargram interpretation, spatial interpolation, and 3-D visualization to map glacier thickness, basal temperate ice, and subglacial channel indicators. Discrete cave-like basal reflectors are further linked using a physically and hydraulically constrained routing scheme. The results indicate that ice thickness increases from the margins and terminus toward a central basin, whereas temperate ice is confined to a basal body beneath the central ablation zone and occupies 39.5% of the surveyed area. On the contrary, mapped caves are concentrated mainly in the lower tongue and near the terminus, with a total connected-path length of ~2 km and an estimated mapped-feature volume of $3.21\times 10 ^{5}$ m3. The lack of directly imaged cave reflectors beneath much of the temperate-ice zone suggests that temperate ice may reduce radar detectability of basal drainage features. These results provide geophysical evidence that LHG12 is not uniformly cold-based but contains a polythermal tongue with an organized subglacial drainage.
item.authors: Tess Xianghuan Luo;Shuang Ye;Min Huang;Tao Pu;Tan Qin;Huaiyuan Zhou;Yushuo Liu;

item.title: Explicit Semantic Transition Modeling for Open-Vocabulary Remote Sensing Change Detection
item.description: Open-vocabulary change detection (OVCD) aims to detect land-cover changes associated with semantic concepts, but existing methods usually infer change semantics from independently predicted endpoint labels. Such endpoint-centric formulations do not directly model semantic change as a directed from-to transition and may suffer from accumulated endpoint errors. In this article, we propose an explicit semantic transition modeling framework for open-vocabulary remote sensing change detection. The proposed method uses frozen DINOv2 and SegEarth-OV3 to extract bi-temporal visual features, semantic probability maps, and text prototypes. A lightweight proposal branch identifies ROIs that may contain changes, within which the model directly predicts pixel-level directed semantic transitions. To handle the large transition space, a compact Top- $k$ candidate set is first constructed from ROI semantic distributions, and a residual candidate supplement module (RCSM) further supplements potentially omitted transitions. Moreover, a consistency-aware semantic transition refinement module (CSTRM) calibrates transition logits through transition-marginal consistency (TMC) and improves spatial coherence through transition-aware refinement. Experiments on six remote sensing change detection datasets demonstrate that the proposed formulation consistently outperforms representative unsupervised, foundation-model-based, and open-vocabulary methods. The code will be available at https://github.com/liuyk97/OV-SCD
item.authors: Yikun Liu;Ying Li;Zhihao Li;Minghao Liu;Gongping Yang;

item.title: Soil Knowledge-Guided Depth-Autoregressive Transformer for Predicting Soil Organic Carbon at Multiple Depths
item.description: The soil organic carbon (SOC) is a critical component of the terrestrial carbon cycle and a key indicator of soil health and agricultural productivity. The accurate prediction of SOC across multiple depths is essential for reliable carbon stock estimation and sustainable soil management. However, the existing approaches still face challenges in achieving high accuracy for deep SOC prediction and often lack the incorporation of soil knowledge, leading to limited model stability, especially for deep soils. To address these issues, we proposed a depth-autoregressive transformer that enhances depth representation through optimized depth embeddings and leverages autoregressive prediction to incorporate prior SOC information from adjacent layers. In addition, a soil knowledge-guided loss (SKG-Loss) was introduced, integrating depth constraints and feature monotonicity constraints to guide the training process. A total of 256 soil cores (0–100 cm) were collected and divided into four depth intervals (0–20, 20–40, 40–60, and 60–100 cm) in this study. Based on multisource environmental covariates, a multitemporal feature set with 32 predictors was developed. The results from location-based fivefold cross-validation demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms five commonly used models, achieving an R2 of 0.69, a root mean square error (RMSE) of 4.11 g kg−1, and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 3.03 g kg−1. The incorporation of SKG-Loss consistently improves prediction accuracy across all depths, with particularly notable gains at 20–60 cm (approximately 10% increase in R ${}^{2}$ ). Finally, the SOC distribution maps at multiple depths with 10-m spatial resolution were generated for the study area. Overall, the proposed approach improves both the accuracy and stability of depthwise SOC prediction, providing an effective and physically informed framework for 3-D SOC mapping and carbon stock assessment.
item.authors: Rui Lu;Hancheng Guo;Zhongxing Chen;Tieming Chen;Zhou Shi;Songchao Chen;

item.title: 3-D Inversion of Loop-Source Semiairborne Transient Electromagnetic Data Incorporating Topographic Effects
item.description: Semiairborne transient electromagnetics (SATEMs) is an emerging geophysical method for mineral exploration, hydrogeological investigations, and engineering applications owing to its high resolution for shallow targets and strong sensitivity to conductive bodies. However, the inherent nonuniqueness of conventional 1-D inversion, together with response distortions induced by topography, can significantly degrade the accuracy and resolution of loop-source SATEM imaging. To address these issues, we develop a 3-D forward and inversion framework that explicitly incorporates topographic effects for SATEM data interpretation. The forward solver uses an unstructured vector finite-element (FE) formulation coupled with an unconditionally stable, second-order backward Euler (SBE) time-stepping scheme, enabling high-fidelity simulations overrugged surfaces. The inversion is accelerated using a limited-memory BFGS algorithm, substantially reducing the computational cost and memory demands associated with sensitivity calculations. Synthetic experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach accurately recovers the geometry and resistivity of subsurface anomalies, and that incorporating topography markedly improves boundary delineation. We further assess the method using two geologically realistic benchmark models: a geological–geophysical model from the Eagle Mountain Mine (USA) and a borehole-constrained model from Voisey’s Bay (Canada).
item.authors: Siyuan Zhang;Junjie Xie;Xinyu Wang;Ri Wang;Siyi Lan;Hongzhu Cai;Xiangyun Hu;

item.title: A Deep Learning Framework for Angular Resolution Enhancement of Multichannel Forward-Looking SAR Under Space-Variant and Perturbed Kernels
item.description: With multiple channels resolving left/right ambiguity, multichannel synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has the ability to perform forward-looking imaging. However, its angular resolution, especially in regions close to the flight path, is limited by the aperture size. In this article, an enhanced imaging scheme under space-variant and perturbed kernels for multichannel forward-looking SAR is proposed. In the scheme, the ideal space-variant convolution matrix is obtained first with the provided system parameters. Then, the linear mapping equation between the preliminary imaging result and the scene is established. The alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is adopted to solve the optimization problem, and the procedure is unrolled into network form. Meanwhile, to overcome the influence of nonideal factors such as residual errors and noise, the influence of a perturbed kernel function is considered by introducing a perturbation factor and synchronously estimating it during iterations, and the plug-and-play (PnP) module with denoising is added to the network. At last, the experimental results are illustrated to verify the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.
item.authors: Wenchao Li;Chengjie Kang;Genghao Zhang;Rui Chen;Junjie Wu;Jianyu Yang;

item.title: A Spaceborne SAR RFI Suppression Method Based on an Adaptive Subband-Forming Technology
item.description: Radio frequency interference (RFI) severely degrades the quality of spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images. The most current methods usually mitigate interference in only a single domain, such as notch filtering (NF) in the frequency domain, beamforming (BF) in the spatial domain, or low-rank and sparse methods in the energy domain. Inspired by BF techniques, this article designs an adaptive subband-forming technology (SFT) model that combines both the frequency and energy domains (EDs) for interference suppression. The proposed technology consists of two processing modes: the model-solving SFT (MS-SFT) mode and the weight-application SFT (WA-SFT) mode. By introducing spectrum division into a low-rank optimization model, the model can be solved by the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) with closed-form updates, and then a signal component, an RFI component, and a set of optimal subband weights can be obtained from the raw polluted SAR data. After solving the proposed model, the optimal subband weights can be applied directly to reconstruct the clean scenes and mitigate the homologous interference (HI) with similar spectral characteristics in other regions without iteration, by using the WA-SFT algorithm. Experiments on Sentinel-1 C-band data and LuTan-1 L-band data demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed MS-SFT and WA-SFT modes.
item.authors: Xuezhi Chen;Yan Huang;Xutao Yu;Jie Li;Yuan Mao;Shuyi Gu;Yanyang Liu;Zaichen Zhang;

item.title: PC-MTPNet With Prototype Constraints for Fine-Grained Rice Classification From Multi-Temporal Polarimetric SAR Images
item.description: Multi-temporal polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (SAR) captures temporal dynamics and polarimetric scattering variations during the rice-growing season, providing critical information for crop growth monitoring and fine-grained rice classification. However, in complex SAR backgrounds, rice fields are often surrounded by water, shoals, and urban built-up areas, while speckle noise and mixed boundaries further hinder accurate fine-grained discrimination. Existing deep segmentation networks typically feed SAR features directly into the model, with limited explicit modeling of the statistical structure of multi-temporal polarimetric features and fine-grained rice categories. They also lack effective constraints on intraclass compactness and interclass separability, leading to substantial confusion between rice subcategories. To address these limitations, this study proposes PC-MTPNet for fine-grained rice classification using multi-temporal full- and compact-polarimetric SAR features. PC-MTPNet integrates the multi-temporal polarimetric statistical descriptor (MTP-Desc), the multi-temporal polarimetric prototype constraint (MTP-Polar), and a detail-refined U-Net++ backbone. A composite loss function is introduced to impose intraclass compactness and interclass separation, while an edge head, boundary loss, and Hann–Gaussian sliding-window fusion are employed to enhance boundary delineation and full-scene inference stability. Experimental results show that PC-MTPNet achieves an overall accuracy (OA), mean intersection over union (mIoU), macro-averaged $F1$ score (Macro-F1), and Kappa of 93.73%, 86.49%, 92.66%, and 92.11%, respectively. Compared with U-Net++, SegFormer-B1, CVNN-PolSAR, and other methods, PC-MTPNet improves these four metrics by at least 3.05, 5.11, 2.80, and 0.55 percentage points, with maximum gains of 11.80, 19.40, 12.83, and 14.72 percentage points, respectively. For direct-sown japonica rice paddy (D-J) and transplanted hybrid rice paddy (T-H), PC-MTPNet achieves classification accuracies of 93.50% and 92.49%, respectively, improving over the U-Net++ baseline by 17.57 and 16.50 percentage points, respectively. These results indicate that multi-temporal polarimetric statistical description and prototype constraints effectively reduce statistical confusion between rice subcategories and improve the robustness of fine-grained rice classification in complex polarimetric SAR scenes.
item.authors: Xianyu Guo;Junming Liang;Junjun Yin;Kun Li;Jian Yang;

item.title: Ground Moving Target Detection in Multichannel Polarization SAR-GMTI Systems
item.description: In this article, a novel ground moving target (GMT) detection algorithm is proposed in a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system based on the space–time-polarization cascaded processing. In the proposed method, the polarization classification is first accomplished based on multipolarization data, followed by spatial domain adaptive processing in the SAR image domain for each polarization channel based on the polarization classification results. Subsequently, the preliminary detection results of moving targets from a single polarization channel can be obtained, and the target polarization steering vectors can be estimated through an iterative process, in order to achieve adaptive coherent synthesis of the target signal in the polarization domain and accomplish the secondary clutter cancellation. Furthermore, a target detection technique based on the polarization distance window detector (PD-DT) is proposed to effectively enhance the detection probability of moving targets and decrease false alarms. Finally, based on the estimated polarization steering vectors of GMTs, adaptive processing in the polarization domain is performed for each spatial channel, greatly improving the output signal-to-clutter-plus-noise ratios (SCNRs) for detected targets, beneficial to the subsequent target relocation. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified using real-measured data from an airborne multichannel fully polarimetric SAR (Pol-SAR) system.
item.authors: Penghui Huang;Junjie Li;Lingyu Wang;Jixia Fan;Jingtao Ma;Jingxian Chen;Yanyang Liu;Guisheng Liao;

item.title: Electro-Optical Response-Aware Learning for PAN-Sharpening of Satellite Images
item.description: Most deep-learning-based panchromatic (PAN)-sharpening methods are trained under simplified and fixed degradation models, typically assuming an isotropic Gaussian point spread function (PSF). However, real electro-optical (EO) satellite systems exhibit scene- and acquisition-dependent blur characteristics caused by diffraction, optical aberrations, platform motion, and intersensor misalignment, which results in a domain gap between synthetic training data and real-world observations. To narrow this gap, we analyze satellite star images and observe that the effective blur is often anisotropic and exhibits extended non-Gaussian residuals. Based on this observation, we propose a PSF prediction network (PSFPN) that estimates a scene-specific PSF consisting of an anisotropic Gaussian component and a residual term. The predicted PSFs quantitatively reveal sensor-dependent EO responses: the mean anisotropy ratios are 1.012, 1.310, and 1.041 for Korea Multi-Purpose Satellite-3A (KOMPSAT-3A), WorldView-II, and QuickBird, respectively. We then use the predicted PSFs to generate physically consistent training data for existing PAN-sharpening networks without changing their inference architectures. To evaluate the effectiveness of our PSFPN, we conducted comparative experiments on four deep-learning-based PAN-sharpening methods trained with fixed PSF-based and PSFPN-based degradation processes. Extensive experiments on multiple satellite datasets show that the PAN-sharpening methods trained with PSFPN-based degradation outperform those trained with fixed PSF-based degradation in both reduced- and full-resolution evaluations, while also enhancing geometric consistency and reducing misregistration-related artifacts. In particular, under the PSFPN-based degradation test protocol, the average peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) values of the four deep-learning-based PAN-sharpening methods trained with our PSFPN-based degradation are higher than those trained with a fixed PSF by 0.6970, 0.9158, and 1.0432 dB on the KOMPSAT-3A, WorldView-II, and QuickBird datasets, respectively. Under the random anisotropic Gaussian-based degradation test protocol, the corresponding average PSNR improvements on the KOMPSAT-3A, WorldView-II, and QuickBird datasets are 0.5058, 0.4900, and 0.5037 dB, respectively, without any additional inference cost.
item.authors: Hyun-Ho Kim;Munchurl Kim;

item.title: Weakly Supervised Hyperspectral Target Detection Based on Contrastive Learning and Graph-Structural Position
item.description: Hyperspectral target detection is significant in remote sensing, yet existing methods heavily rely on strong supervision. Target prior spectra are sensitive to illumination, atmospheric, and sensor variations, causing inevitable deviations that degrade performance. Pixel-level annotations are prohibitively costly due to high spatial resolution and subpixel localization difficulties. Multiple instance learning enables weakly supervised detection using region-level labels, but most existing methods neglect spatial dependencies among pixels and suffer from limited localization capability. To address these issues, this article proposes a graph-structured positional transformer for multiple-instance learning (GSPT-MIL), a graph-structured and position-aware weakly supervised multiple-instance learning (MIL) method that achieves accurate pixel-level detection using only bag-level labels, without requiring target priors or pixel-level annotations. The method performs iterative optimization under an expectation-maximization (EM) framework. The expectation step (E-step) infers target locations via a local similarity graph convolution module (LS-GCM) that models spatial dependencies, while the maximization step (M-step) fuses absolute position information via a multiscale contextual position encoder and enhances feature discriminability via a spectral–spatial feature alignment network (SS-FAN). Extensive experiments demonstrate that GSPT-MIL consistently outperforms existing weakly supervised and conventional detection methods, validating its effectiveness and superiority.
item.authors: Ying Cui;Xiaoqi Ren;Liguo Wang;Haifeng Zhu;Zhongwei Shen;Chunhui Zhao;

item.title: Reconstructing Multiangular Field HCRF Spectra From Indoor Measurements via a Spectral–Frequency–Global Network
item.description: Recovering physically consistent reflectance from spectra affected by systematic measurement errors remains a fundamental challenge in quantitative remote sensing, especially when the observation process is only partially modeled. In indoor semiphysical, multiangular measurement systems, residual discrepancies persist between indoor hemispherical-conical reflectance factor (HCRF) measurements and outdoor field observations because of illumination mismatch, geometric uncertainty, and instrument-induced spectral distortions. To address this problem, this article formulates indoor-to-field correction as an angle-aware spectral reconstruction task and proposes a data-driven framework termed the spectral–frequency–global network (SFGNet). The network jointly models local spectral features, long-range spectral dependencies, frequency-domain residual patterns, and observation geometry, enabling the correction of both radiometric bias and spectral-shape distortion under anisotropic conditions. Extensive experiments on paired indoor–outdoor HCRF measurements of multiple mineral samples show that, compared with raw indoor observations, SFGNet directly reduces the average mean squared error (mse) by 75.4% and increases the spectral correlation coefficient (SCC) from 0.9024 to 0.9595. Further analyses demonstrate improved angular anisotropy reconstruction and robust spatiotemporal generalization to independent field samples. These results demonstrate that geometry-aware data-driven correction effectively enhances the field consistency of indoor HCRF measurements and supports high-accuracy optical remote sensing simulation.
item.authors: Guorui Jia;Honglin Ji;Huijie Zhao;Feixiang Wang;Zhen Li;Xianfei Qiu;Xiaoshuang Wu;Yinuo Wang;

item.title: Hardness-Aware Contrastive Learning With Data Condensation for Open-Set Hyperspectral Image Classification
item.description: In recent years, hyperspectral image classification (HSIC) has been widely applied in precision agriculture, environmental monitoring, and remote sensing. However, the frequent emergence of unknown categories, such as novel land-cover types and anomalous regions, poses significant challenges to traditional closed-set classifiers. Open-set classification seeks to accurately recognize known classes while rejecting unknown ones, but existing methods are often limited by high intraclass spectral variability, insufficient exploitation of hard samples, and imprecise class representations. To overcome these challenges, this article proposes an open-set detection framework called HACL-DC, which combines hardness-aware contrastive learning with soft-label-weighted data condensation. The framework consists of three key components. First, a similarity contrastive weighting module enhances contrastive learning by assigning higher weights to hard intraclass positives and interclass negatives through linear transformations combined with sigmoid and inverse-sigmoid functions, promoting compact intraclass features and stronger interclass separation. Second, a soft-label-weighted condensation algorithm (SWCA) constructs compact etalon sets for each known class by leveraging soft-label assignment, dual-parameter gradient optimization, and adaptive etalon resetting to capture fine-grained class distributions and local density information. Finally, weighted similarities between test samples and class etalons are computed using etalon influence scores, enabling accurate known-class classification and effective detection of out-of-distribution (OOD) samples. Extensive experiments on three public hyperspectral datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed HACL-DC framework.
item.authors: Hanyue Wang;Wei Liu;Jing Zhao;Xianghai Cao;Licheng Jiao;

item.title: WF-Mamba: Weighted Fourier State-Space Models With Adaptive Spatial-Frequency Synergy for Hyperspectral Unmixing
item.description: Hyperspectral unmixing (HU) is a crucial technique that aims to estimate subpixel-level ground object information in remote sensing images. Existing deep learning-based unmixing methods, especially autoencoders (AEs), typically operate only within the original spatial–spectral feature domain. However, due to the impact of noise and spectral variability, relying solely on the original domain makes it difficult to fully extract effective features and leaves the models highly susceptible to interference. To address these issues, we present an innovative dual-stream spatial-frequency state-space model (SSM), termed WF-Mamba, for enhanced HU. A physics-driven snake-like scanning (SS) mechanism is introduced in WF-Mamba to remodel the data serialization process, which strictly preserves the intrinsic neighborhood contiguity and 2-D topological priors. To extend the feature domain and overcome the frequency-domain blindness of pure spatial models, a macroscopic weighted Fourier neural operator (WFNO) branch is constructed. By dynamically recalibrating global low-frequency modes in the complex domain, WFNO functions as an advanced physical filter to actively suppress high-frequency noise. Furthermore, an adaptive synergistic fusion (ASF) mechanism is proposed for WF-Mamba to break the bottleneck of rigid feature concatenation. More robust features can be obtained by ASF by autonomously balancing the sharp local spatial boundaries extracted by Mamba with the globally purified smoothness from WFNO via dynamic residual gating. The fused robust features are then mapped to estimate accurate abundances and reconstruct the image. Extensive experiments on one synthetic and three real hyperspectral datasets demonstrate that the proposed WF-Mamba achieves competitive performance compared to advanced methods.
item.authors: Lianhui Liang;Jinrong Chen;Shaoquan Zhang;Bing Tu;Jun Li;Antonio Plaza;

item.title: DDFGFormer: Dual-Decoupled Frequency-Guided Transformer for Hyperspectral Image Classification
item.description: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification requires jointly capturing subtle spectral differences and complex spatial structures. Recent studies have introduced frequency-domain modeling to complement spatial–spectral representation learning. However, existing frequency-based methods still face some limitations. First, most methods mainly focus on amplitude or energy distributions while insufficiently exploiting phase information for structural localization and edge representation. In addition, raw phase information is sensitive to noise, smooth regions, and mixed pixels, which may introduce unreliable interference. Furthermore, spatial–frequency interaction is often implemented through simple posterior fusion, failing to use frequency-domain priors to actively guide spatial feature extraction. To address these limitations, we propose a dual-decoupled frequency-guided transformer, termed DDFGFormer, for HSI classification. In particular, we design a frequency-guided transformer block (FGTB) composed of dual-decoupled frequency attention (DDFA) and a frequency-enhanced feed-forward network (FEFFN). DDFA decouples the Fourier representation into amplitude and phase, and further decomposes the amplitude into high- and low-frequency components, thereby explicitly capturing amplitude- and phase-aware cues. To suppress unreliable phase responses, an amplitude-prior guided phase (APGP) module contained in DDFA is proposed to adaptively modulate phase representations and transform raw phase into stable structural priors. Furthermore, FEFFN injects frequency-domain information into feature propagation, enabling frequency priors to actively recalibrate spatial features rather than serving only as posterior fusion cues. Extensive experiments on four HSI datasets show that DDFGFormer outperforms nine state-of-the-art methods in overall accuracy (OA), average accuracy (AA), kappa, and boundary $F1$ -score (BF1), with OA gains of 1.65%, 1.63%, 1.25%, and 1.14% over the second-best method on Indian Pines (IPs), Pavia University (PU), Salinas (SAs), and WHU-Hi-LongKou (LK), respectively.
item.authors: Jinliang An;Dengru Han;Longlong Dai;Weidong Zhang;Xiangrong Zhang;

item.title: GeoSelect: Spatial-Program Execution for Training-Free Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation
item.description: Referring remote sensing image segmentation (RRSIS) segments the object named by a natural-language expression in an aerial image. Existing training-free methods resolve the expression through implicit vision–language activations or region–text similarity, which gives weak control over the spatial, superlative, and ordinal relations that dominate aerial referring, such as the rightmost ship or the second court from the left. We propose GeoSelect, a training-free pipeline that reframes referring as the execution of a typed spatial program. A frozen, text-only language model synthesizes the expression into a small domain-specific language (DSL), a well-formedness checker accepts the program, and a deterministic executor runs it. The central abstraction is a single scored candidate set type under which every operator composes: continuous geometric fields realize position and proximity, while discrete set and order operators add the extremum, ordinal, top- $k$ , and relational constructions that fields alone cannot express. Execution is explicit, so every intermediate is inspectable, and a reliability ladder degrades any failing program to the field-only special case. GeoSelect achieves 58.86 mIoU on RRSIS-D test and 55.27 mIoU on RISBench test, more than twice the best prior training-free method on RRSIS-D, with no referring supervision and on a single GPU. Under a fixed detector and segmenter, explicit execution improves over implicit selectors under the same backbone; the best-box-IoU and outcome-partition diagnostics motivate complementary tests of proposal recall and program-path behavior, with the program path the clearer priority on RISBench, and an exposure audit shows comparable accuracy on the audited unseen subset. Code and configurations are available at https://github.com/Avalon-S/GeoSelect
item.authors: Yuhang Jiang;Guohui Deng;Miaozhong Xu;Chao Ruan;Jinling Zhao;Linsheng Huang;

item.title: BCAP: Black-Box Cross-Modal Adversarial Patch Attacks Against Multimodal Vehicle Recognition Systems via UAV Remote Sensing
item.description: The reliability of deep learning-based object detection in uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing increasingly relies on fusing visible and infrared sensors. However, existing attack methods used to evaluate their robustness are often unrealistic, assuming white-box access or targeting only a single modality. This article first reveals a critical cross-modal vulnerability through region sensitivity analysis on various YOLO detectors, demonstrating that both visible and infrared models exhibit a shared spatial weakness by being most sensitive to perturbations in the target vehicle’s central area. Leveraging this key insight, we propose a framework with black-box cross-modal adversarial patch (BCAP) attacks on UAV detectors. BCAP introduces a multiobjective optimization formulation that models visible and infrared modalities as independent yet competing objectives, which enables effective cross-modal optimization without manual weight tuning. It employs a novel grid-constrained Bezier curve generation method to efficiently search for smooth, effective patch shapes within this sensitive central region, further enhanced by an adaptive population restart strategy. Extensive experiments on the DroneVehicle dataset show BCAP achieves a 50%–61% cross-modal attack success rate (ASR), significantly outperforming the 37%–42% range of existing methods. This work provides a more potent and realistic baseline for evaluating the end-to-end reliability of multimodal UAV remote sensing systems.
item.authors: Jiayi Wang;Hua Han;Kaiyu Xu;Li Huang;

item.title: Scale-Consistent Multispectral Reconstruction From UAV and Satellite Observations for Coastal Bathymetric Inversion
item.description: High-resolution quantitative remote sensing is constrained by the spatial–spectral trade-off among current observation platforms: uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery provides fine spatial detail but limited spectral dimensionality, whereas satellite multispectral data provide richer spectral information at coarser spatial scales. This study proposes data-driven spectral-structural anchoring fusion (DSSAF), a scale-consistent framework that reconstructs UAV-scale multispectral imagery by integrating fine-resolution structural information from UAV RGB imagery with multispectral constraints from PlanetScope observations. The framework combines land-cover-conditioned spectral mapping, data-driven structural reference selection, adaptive detail injection, and scale-consistency correction. It was evaluated over a heterogeneous intertidal sandbar system and further tested through shallow-water bathymetric inversion. The reconstructed imagery preserved UAV-scale textures, gradients, and edges while remaining radiometrically consistent with the original PlanetScope data after reaggregation to the native satellite scale. In the downstream bathymetry task, DSSAF-fused imagery achieved the best performance among the tested inputs, with R ${}^{2} =0.924$ and RMSE = 0.079 m. These results demonstrate that scale-consistent UAV-satellite fusion can improve both image-level spatial–spectral representation and quantitative geophysical retrieval, providing a transferable approach for high-resolution environmental mapping in heterogeneous coastal landscapes.

item.title: AMS-SemiCD: A Synergistic Framework for Semisupervised Change Detection via an Adaptive Pseudolabeling Strategy and a Multibranch Network
item.description: Semisupervised change detection (SSCD) aims to reduce the dependence on extensive labeled data. However, existing methods face three critical challenges. First, class imbalance and boundary ambiguity induce class-dependent confidence distributions, hindering reliable pseudolabel selection. Second, uncertain pixels may still contain useful structural cues, while their indiscriminate use can amplify pseudolabel noise. Third, achieving complementary local–global feature representations in dual-branch architectures typically incurs prohibitive computational costs. To address these issues, we propose the adaptive multibranch synergistic SSCD (AMS-SemiCD) framework, which uses teacher–student consistency regularization to supervise unlabeled bitemporal pairs. Within this framework, the adaptive statistical pseudolabel refinement (ASPR) strategy improves the reliability and utilization of consistency targets through class-adaptive dynamic thresholding and contribution-adaptive soft weighting. As a result, ASPR accommodates class-dependent confidence distributions while effectively exploiting uncertain but informative pixels. Meanwhile, the multibranch synergistic enhancement network (MSE-Net) enhances discriminative feature representation by integrating local CNN and global Mamba branches with manageable computational costs. Specifically, MSE-Net consists of the multibranch spatiotemporal synergistic fusion (MSSF) for local–global fusion, the multibranch spatiotemporal difference booster (MSDB) for temporal-difference enhancement, and the adaptive gated attention refiner (AGAR) for cross-layer refinement. Extensive experiments on the GoogleGZ-CD, WHU-CD, and LEVIR-CD datasets demonstrate that AMS-SemiCD consistently outperforms advanced SSCD methods. Notably, with only 20% labeled data on LEVIR-CD, our method achieves an $F1$ score of 91.17% and an intersection over union (IoU) of 83.78%. The code will be available at https://github.com/RSII-NWNUAMS-SemiCD

item.title: A Growth-Prior-Informed Forest Age Estimation Method Using Overlapping ICESat/GLAS and GEDI Footprints With Reduced Dependence on Field Calibration Data
item.description: Forest age is a critical ecological variable for quantifying carbon sequestration, assessing biodiversity, and supporting sustainable forest management. Conventional remote sensing approaches for forest age estimation either rely heavily on field inventory data or require long-term optical archives, limiting their scalability and applicability across diverse forest types and age ranges. This study presented a novel light detection and ranging (LiDAR)-based framework that leverages the temporal complementarity of the Ice, Cloud, and land Elevation Satellite/Geoscience Laser Altimeter System (ICESat/GLAS, 2003–2009) and the Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI, 2019-present). By reformulating classical height-age growth models into a temporally paired-height structure, canopy height at the later observation was expressed as a function of canopy height at the earlier observation and the elapsed time interval. Overlapping GLAS and GEDI footprints provide paired canopy height observations spanning more than a decade, enabling direct parameterization of growth models with reduced dependence on field-derived age calibration data. The framework was evaluated in two ecologically distinct regions. For Larix gmelinii in Northeast China, the estimated ages achieved an R2 of 0.86 with a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 13.37 years. For loblolly pine in the southeastern United States, the corresponding R2 and RMSE were 0.71 and 5.74 years, respectively. Further simulations with random height measurement errors confirmed the resilience of the model, demonstrating strong robustness for loblolly pine and relative stability for L. gmelinii, with increased sensitivity only in later growth stages. Building on these results, the models were applied at the regional scale to generate 30 m resolution forest age maps for both study areas. At the regional scale, the estimated mean age in Study Area I was 55.8 years, broadly consistent with the estimates from two independent national products (59.6 and 64.5 years), and the young-forest proportion was 16.4%. In Study Area II, map-derived ages showed strong agreement with stand-level observations (R ${}^{2} =0.96$ , RMSE = 2.83 years). Overall, this LiDAR-driven framework substantially reduces dependence on dense field calibration and long-term optical time series, offering a complementary pathway for full-spectrum forest age estimation.

item.title: Residual Multiple Suppression Using a Physics-Informed Plug-In Network With Residual-Multiple-Level Prior
item.description: Multiple suppression is a fundamental problem in seismic processing because residual multiples often exhibit kinematic characteristics similar to those of primary reflections, making these interfering events hard to remove cleanly in practice. As a result, conventional methods usually face a tradeoff: aggressive parameter settings tend to damage useful primaries, whereas conservative settings often leave residual multiple energy insufficiently attenuated. To address this issue, this article presents a physics-informed plug-in network for residual multiple suppression. Instead of replacing conventional demultiple pipelines, the proposed method takes preliminary demultiple results as input and performs targeted refinement on the remaining residual multiples. The framework first estimates a physics-guided residual-multiple-level prior to characterize the spatial distribution of residual contamination. This prior then guides an attention-based attenuation network to apply spatially varying suppression strength. In addition, an optional geological-structure-guided recovery step can further return primary-consistent energy from the removed component. For training, samples are adaptively synthesized from real-data-derived primary and residual-multiple proxies. In this way, the method preserves compatibility with existing industrial workflows while improving the balance between residual attenuation and primary preservation. Experiments on synthetic and field data show that the proposed method suppresses residual multiple energy more effectively than conventional baselines while better preserving the continuity and amplitude consistency of primary reflections.
item.authors: Zhiyu Yao;Wenkai Lu;Weiheng Geng;Jinpeng Liu;Mingrui Zhong;Yili Ren;

item.title: Adaptive-Dictionary-Regularized 3-D Direct Inversion of Surface-Wave Dispersion Data
item.description: Conventional global smoothing regularization suppresses velocity anomaly amplitudes and blurs structural boundaries in regions of sparse ray coverage, limiting fine-scale crustal imaging under nonuniform observational conditions. This study introduces local sparse regularization based on adaptive-dictionary learning into the DSurfTomo 3-D direct inversion framework, yielding the DSurfTomo-local sparse tomography (LST) method, which simultaneously characterizes smooth velocity backgrounds and discontinuous structural boundaries. Under a Bayesian maximum a posteriori (MAP) formulation, the method couples the global $L_{2}$ constraint and a local dictionary sparsity prior in a unified objective function and jointly solves for the velocity model and sparse coefficients via alternating minimization. During the inversion iterations, dictionary atoms are updated in synchrony with the velocity model using the iterative thresholding and signed K-means (ITKM) algorithm, ensuring that the sparsity regularization remains consistent with the local structure of the current velocity field throughout the inversion. Synthetic data tests demonstrate that, relative to DSurfTomo, DSurfTomo-LST significantly improves velocity anomaly amplitude recovery and structural-boundary resolution under sparse ray-coverage conditions, with the overall root-mean-square error (RMSE) reduced by approximately 38% and 22% in the checkerboard and spike tests, respectively. Applications to the ChinArray data recover velocity structures consistent with regional tectonic features. The Luzhou dense-array results show velocity anomalies whose spatial distribution broadly corresponds to structural features observed in the seismic reflection profile.
item.authors: Zhiwen Li;Jianyang Ding;Xiaoyan Cheng;Renjie He;Xiaohua Zhou;Zubin Chen;

item.title: A Simplified Analysis of Full-Waveform Inversion (FWI) With Optimal Transport
item.description: Full-waveform inversion (FWI) is a key seismic imaging method, posed as a nonlinear optimization problem to recover high-resolution subsurface models. Its usual least-squares ( $L^{2}$ ) misfit, however, often converges to local minima because of the objective’s strong nonconvexity and cycle skipping. To mitigate this, recent work explores optimal transport (OT)-based misfits, particularly the squared Wasserstein-2 distance ( $W_{2}^{2}$ ), which has better convexity properties. This article analytically characterizes this metric by deriving a simplified 1-D expression for the gradient of $W_{2}^{2}$ under assumptions relevant to early-stage FWI. This enables a direct quantitative comparison between $W_{2}^{2}$ and $L^{2}$ gradients and clarifies the theoretical advantages of the Wasserstein metric for estimating acoustic velocity in homogeneous regions, improving FWI robustness and efficiency.
